question: Why is there no rejection even amid the activity of creation and the rest?
premises: Even amid the activity of creation and the rest, the yogin does not reject, owing to knower-ness.
Knower-ness is relish of the turya wonder, a perceiving that lets nothing unshone.
The cited passage confirms indestructibility through absence of rise and fall.
inference: Turya-relish knower-ness lets the yogin sustain all activity without rejection.
plain_english: Even amid the activity of creation and the rest, there is no rejection, owing to knower-ness: the yogin, of turya-wonder relish and perceiving nature, does not waver, since in the absence of rejection nothing remains unshone, as the cited passage confirms of the imperishable self whose rise and fall are absent.
